Subject: Discovery recap & open items — CoreMedica pilot

Hi Kari / Evan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we keep momentum toward a pilot: 

Call highlights (30m):
- Use case: ingesting and normalizing physician notes for downstream analytics and triage automation.
- Target scope: 5M tokens/month to start; latency SLO ~250ms p95 for single-turn queries.
- Decision criteria: security/compliance (SOC 2 + pen test), predictable unit cost, data residency, and API-level observability.

Stakeholder map (from conversation):
- Economic buyer: Kari Sullivan (CFO) — controls budget and approves PO.
- InfoSec lead: Evan Liu — responsible for security evidence and scoping of tests.
- Procurement: procurement@coremedica.com — handles PO/terms.
- Legal: TBD (we'll loop them in for standard T&Cs / DPA).

Open items / asks (what we will deliver):
1) Redacted SOC 2 Type II report (sensitive op details removed) — deliver by end of day Thu (11/19).
2) Pen test executive summary and remediation posture — deliver Thu (11/19).
3) Sample audit log extract (redacted) showing timestamps, event types, and tenant IDs — deliver within 24 hours of request.
4) Written answers for data retention, deletion, KMS, and SIEM forwarding options — included with docs.
5) Procurement timeline & template PO expectations from your side.

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood to send SOC2 + pen test summary + data-retention Q&A by 11/19 EOD.
- Schedule follow-up call with Kari + Evan + Procurement + Redwood on Fri 11/20 @ 14:00 PT to review evidence and procurement path.

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — that aligns with our discussion. A couple clarifications from procurement and finance: 

1) Procurement timeline: target to complete vendor review and issue PO by Dec 10, assuming security sign-off. Procurement will need SOC2 and pen test artifacts to attach to the vendor file.
2) Redaction: please ensure all internal IP and customer-specific examples are redacted from SOC2 and pen test docs — procurement will not accept raw findings that mention third parties.
3) Data retention question: we typically require a default retention of 30 days for hot logs and a bridging option to archive longer-term if needed. Can your platform support configurable retention windows per tenant?
4) SIEM: we will want log export (or forward) into our Splunk instance — provide the supported ingestion patterns.

I'll be on the 11/20 slot as proposed; Evan will lead the security review portion.

Kari Sullivan
CFO | CoreMedica
kari@coremedica.com

Hi Kari / Evan — Monica from Solutions/Trust here. Per Diego's note, attaching the items we can share now (redacted):

Attachments (redacted stubs):
- Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026_redacted.pdf (redacted control descriptions)
- Redwood_PenTest_Summary_2026_redacted.pdf (exec summary + critical/important findings and status)
- AuditLog_Schema_sample.csv (sample rows with tenant_id, event_type, timestamp, ip, redacted_user)

Answers to the specific asks:
- Data retention: configurable retention windows per tenant. Default hot retention: 30 days; configurable up to 90 days in-platform. For longer-term retention we offer an export pipeline to a customer-managed bucket (S3/GCS) or an archival service.
- SIEM forwarding: we can stream audit events to customer SIEMs via a secure push connector (TLS + mTLS optional). We also support S3 export and a Kafka-compatible push.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported for data encryption at rest; keys can be rotated per your policy.
- Pen test: the attached summary covers external blackbox testing and internal config checks; we can provide more detail under NDA if procurement/legal require it.

We will prepare a 2-page audit-log sample with real timestamps (redacted PII) and share it by EOD today. Let us know the preferred ingestion format for your Splunk team.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

Thanks Monica — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few follow-ups from InfoSec: 

1) Audit log sample: please include at least 48 hours of events (time-ordered) with UTC timestamps, event name, resource identifiers, and tenant IDs. Redact usernames/emails but keep event semantics and IP ranges intact.
2) Pen test scope: can you confirm whether the summary represents an external/internet-facing assessment only, or if it includes authenticated/privileged testing of runtime components? We'll need scope to understand coverage.
3) CVE remediation: for any findings in the pen test summary, provide the current remediation status and CVE references where applicable.

Procurement: Kari, looping you so you have visibility.

Evan Liu
